text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - Shares finished up, helped by three-straight Wall Street advances. But the FTSE's near-term upside potential is seen limited as investors fear interest rates will need to be increased in order to curb a booming British economy. The FTSE 100 closed 23.0 points up to 4,292.3.

FRANKFURT - The share market continued its process of recovery after falling heavily last week, but lacked volumes and new data to drive it back into record territory. The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in 30 German blue-chips, ended the day at 3,364.76 points, up 36.63 points or 1.10 percent, boosted by early strength on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street. Earlier, the 30-share DAX index ended at 3,359.46 points, up 29.70 points or 0.89 percent.

PARIS - Stocks closed sharply higher in a rally triggered by the gains on Wall Street. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 38.55 points, or 1.49 percent, at 2,617.55. The index finished off its session highs after Wall Street snapped its rising streak in early trading, but brokers said the bourse was sustained by expectations that the franc's strength left scope for a French interest rate cut.

ZURICH - Shares gained more than one percent in active trade as Novartis and Winterthur Insurance led the market higher. Dealers said market sentiment seemed to have changed as many investors who had stayed away were now rushing back to the market. The Broad SPI closed up 30.82 points to 2,929.78.

TOKYO - Stocks ended trade with hefty losses brought on by continued selling of financial sector shares and profit-taking of some bellwether issues which had rallied on Tuesday. The 225-share Nikkei average finished 318.33 points or 1.77 percent lower at 17,703.37.

HONG KONG - Blue chips ended with only moderate gains as this week's rebound in prices began to slow, but China plays rallied amid a lack of interest in big cap stocks and strength in mainland markets. The Hang Seng Index rose 28.11 points, or 0.23 percent, to close at 12,426.68.

SYDNEY - The share market locked in solid gains by the close as buyers returned to the market in numbers after the release of the Wallis report into the financial system. The All Ordinaries index jumped 20.3 points to close at 2,389.2.

JOHANNESBURG - Confined to mostly narrow trading ranges, stocks ended a touch above overnight closing levels despite a slip in gold shares towards the finish. Dealers said the market had shown no clear direction, although the underlying sentiment remained positive amid some genuine demand for stock, especially blue-chips later in the day. At the close the industrial index was up 5.2 points to 8,249.9 hoisting the all-share index up 4.3 points to 7,048.4. Gold stocks were a non-event again with the index finishing off 9.2 points at 1,309.1.
